name: vol_adjusted_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the 5-minute realized volatility (last 60 bars) is compressing relative to the 30-minute baseline (last 360 bars), the dominant flow shifts from momentum algos and stop-cascade sellers to VWAP-benchmarked institutional accumulators who continuously pull price back toward their benchmark. In this regime, even a 1.5-sigma deviation from the 10-minute rolling mean becomes statistically meaningful and rapidly reverts. The adaptive threshold (wider in turbulent periods, tighter in calm) prevents entering during trending vol-expansion events where NIFTY deviations extend rather than revert. When RSI confirms oversold/overbought in a vol-compressing regime, institutional TWAP replenishment kicks in within 30-60 seconds creating the snap-back.

indicators.name: price_z
indicators.purpose: 10-minute rolling z-score (120 bars × 5s). At 5s bars holding 30-90s, the 10-min window defines 'where the mean is right now' — long enough to smooth noise, short enough to be current. The original used 60 1-min bars (60 min window) which was the context for 10-60 min holds; we compress to 10 min because we're trading the fast reversion, not the slow drift.

indicators.name: vol_fast
indicators.purpose: 5-minute realized volatility (60 bars). Fast component of vol ratio. Maps to original's 30-bar vol on 1-min bars (30 min), but compressed to 5 min because we need to detect vol compression at a timescale relevant to our 30-90s hold — if vol has been expanding in the last 5 min, our entry is premature.

indicators.name: vol_slow
indicators.purpose: 30-minute realized volatility (360 bars). Slow context for the vol ratio. Maps directly from original's 120-bar vol on 1-min bars (120 min) — compressed 4x to 30 min because intraday vol regime shifts are faster on an index than on individual stocks.

indicators.name: vol_ratio
indicators.purpose: Ratio of 5-min vol to 30-min vol. When < 1.0 vol is compressing (calm regime, reversion works well). When > 1.5, vol is expanding (trending/momentum regime, avoid mean-reversion). This is the adaptive scaling mechanism ported directly from original.

indicators.name: adaptive_threshold
indicators.purpose: Dynamic z-score entry threshold: tight (~1.5) in calm periods, wide (~2.3) in turbulent periods. Prevents entering against momentum moves disguised as mean-reversion setups.

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute RSI (36 bars × 5s) for directional confirmation. Original used RSI(14) on 1-min = 14-min RSI. Compressed to 3 min because we're catching the fast oversold/overbought extreme, not a slow trend exhaustion. 36 bars is long enough to form a meaningful oscillator at 5s frequency without aliasing noise.

conditions: price_z < -adaptive_threshold (price below vol-adjusted mean by enough sigma)
rsi_36 < rsi_extreme (oversold at 3-min scale confirms selling pressure exhausted)
vol_ratio < vol_ratio_limit (vol is not wildly expanding — mean reversion regime)
buy_ce.confirmation: price_z turns up from the extreme (cross above threshold - 0.2)

conditions: price_z > adaptive_threshold (price above vol-adjusted mean by enough sigma)
buy_pe.confirmation: price_z turns down from the extreme

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. For a 30-90s mean-reversion trade, if NIFTY extends 8 spot points further away from the mean (rather than reverting), the z-score has deepened another 0.5+ sigma and the institutional replenishment thesis has failed. Consistent with 2-minute typical NIFTY move of 5-10 pts — we exit before the 90th percentile adverse move.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option points = ~12 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. A 1.5-2.5 sigma deviation from a 10-min mean on NIFTY typically represents 15-25 spot points; capturing 12 points (50-60% of the overshoot) within 90 seconds is the median first-leg reversion. Consistent with the 1-minute typical NIFTY move of 3-7 option pts, targeting the upper end given the adaptive filter selects only high-quality setups.

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22 (high-VIX environments have trending deviations that don't revert at 30-90s scale)
filters.time_filter: 09:25-15:20 IST; skip first 10 min (vol_ratio unstable, insufficient lookback for 360-bar slow vol)
filters.trend_filter: vol_ratio < 1.5 (same as ADX < 30 equivalent — rejects trending environments)
filters.spread_filter: not applicable (limit orders at close price)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — adaptive threshold is a structural improvement over static z-scores; NIFTY TWAP institutional flow is persistent

adaptation_notes: Original was on NIFTY50 individual stocks with 1-min bars holding 10-60 min. Key changes: (1) Lookbacks compressed from 60-min/30-min/120-min to 10-min/5-min/30-min because we hold 30-90s instead of 10-60 min — the z-score must be computed over a window relevant to our hold time. (2) RSI compressed from 14-min to 3-min to detect fast extremes. (3) Universe changed from 20-stock filtered universe to NIFTY index itself — no stock-specific filters (delivery %, spread, earnings skip) needed. (4) Vol_ratio limit retained at 1.5 for regime filter. (5) VWAP removed (available on spot_df as a computable indicator but redundant given price_z from SMA captures the same deviation). (6) Stops/targets set in option points calibrated to 30-90s NIFTY move sizes.
weaknesses: At 5s bars, rolling_std computation is noisier than at 1-min bars — the vol_ratio threshold may be less reliable
In NIFTY, mean-reversion at 30-90s can be overridden by sudden macro news (Fed, RBI) causing deviations to extend rather than revert
The adaptive_threshold formula (1.5 + 0.8 * vol_ratio) preserves the original's ad-hoc coefficients; these may need calibration for 5s NIFTY dynamics specifically
Requires 360 bars (30 min) warmup — no trades in the first 30 min of session
